title: Topical PDRN (salmon-DNA polymer) versus retinol: a periocular trial with cell and ex vivo data
headline: A topical PDRN eye cream beat an identical 0.1% retinol cream on wrinkle and dermal-thickness measures over 4 weeks in 31 sensitive-skinned Chinese women, but the authors are company-linked, there was no vehicle-only arm, and nothing here speaks to deep skin or pigment.
evidenceTier: Small split-face RCT (active comparator, 4 weeks) + cell, ex vivo and single-volunteer penetration work. Full text (open access) read
fit: Partial. The cell and ex vivo work is mechanism-level and not skin-tone specific as far as I know, but the one clinical trial was 31 Chinese women (phototype not reported), measured wrinkles and dermal thickness rather than pigment, and compared against retinol, not a prescription retinoid.
displaces: A PDRN step if the routine already has one (a swap, not an addition). It does not replace a prescription retinoid: the comparator was over-the-counter retinol.

cost.label: All markets
cost.value: No retail product matched to the tested material was identified; retail PDRN prices not checked this run

buzzCheck: PDRN is heavily marketed. I did not check retail products this run, so I cannot say whether price tracks evidence. The practical question for any product is the PDRN percentage and fragment length, which are rarely disclosed.
summaryPoints: Design (full text read): randomized, double-blind, split-face, 31 healthy Chinese women aged 35-55 with self-reported sensitive skin. One eye area got a water-in-silicone cream with 0.1% PDRN-850K (salmon-derived DNA, average molecular weight up to 850 kDa); the other got an identical cream with 0.1% retinol. Twice daily for 28 days, daily sunscreen required.

Reported result: at day 28 crow's-feet wrinkle area and number fell by about 20-23% on the PDRN side versus about 6-7% on the retinol side. Ultrasound dermal thickness and density, tear-trough and eye-bag measures, and elasticity and firmness were reported as roughly 1.8 to 2 times greater. Exact values are in figures I could not read numerically.

What weakens it: there was no vehicle-only arm, so the study cannot show PDRN beats a plain cream; 4 weeks is early for retinol; the authors themselves say early ultrasound changes may partly reflect plumping or hydration. Authors are affiliated with companies (a skin-aging research institute and a biotech firm) and the PDRN was supplied by a manufacturer; I did not see a conflict-of-interest statement in the text I read.

The penetration evidence is indirect: Raman signal in a lab-grown epidermis, a porcine skin experiment at 0.1% in solution, and one human volunteer whose forearm showed a relative signal of about 3% at 24 hours. The authors state Raman cannot separate added PDRN from the skin's own nucleic acids.
toneData: Not reported. Trial population was Chinese women; phototype was not stated in the text I read.
fitLine: Interesting mechanism and a head-to-head against retinol, but no vehicle arm, supplier-linked, and no deep-skin data.
timeline: Instrument differences reported from day 14 to day 28; nothing beyond 4 weeks

fitAxes.why: Tolerated by a sensitive-skin cohort with no adverse reactions reported, but the trial did not measure barrier function (no water-loss readings).
Tested against retinol, never alongside it, so I cannot say whether it adds to a retinoid or lets you cut one back.
Not assessed; the tested cream was an eye cream in a water-in-silicone base.
Trial dates were late September to October 2025; no seasonal analysis.

dossier.whatItIs: PDRN (polydeoxyribonucleotide) is a mix of DNA fragments, here a salmon-derived preparation of 96% purity or more with an average molecular weight up to 850 kDa (about 1,200 base pairs), called PDRN-850K by the authors. It is best known as an injectable skin booster. This paper tests it as a cream.

steps: In cultured human dermal fibroblasts, PDRN-850K raised phosphorylation of PI3K and AKT, TGF-beta and SMAD2/3, and autophagy markers (LC3-II up, p62 down). Blocking each pathway with an inhibitor reduced the rise in collagen and elastin gene expression (n=3 experiments).

Delivery: Raman signal rose over 2, 6 and 24 hours in a lab-grown epidermis and fell with an endocytosis inhibitor; fluorescent-labelled PDRN at 0.1% in solution reached the dermis of pig skin by 8-12 hours; in one volunteer, the eye cream showed signal beyond 20 micrometres at 8-24 hours.
In UV-damaged human ex vivo skin (n=3), the 0.1% cream increased viable epidermal thickness and staining for collagens I, III, IV, V, VI, VII, XV, XVII, XVIII, elastin, fibrillin-1 and YAP.
In the split-face trial, wrinkle, dermal-thickness and elasticity measures changed more on the PDRN side than the retinol side.
mechanism.inferenceFlag: The pathway chain (PI3K-Akt, TGF-beta/Smad, autophagy to matrix genes) comes from cells, and pathway activation was tested in unstressed fibroblasts, not UV-damaged ones. That the cream delivers enough intact PDRN into dermis in living human skin is not shown. The authors call their own penetration data supportive, not conclusive.
mechanism.diagramCaption: Cream applied -> signal in viable skin (indirect) -> fibroblast pathways up in cells -> more matrix proteins in ex vivo skin -> better wrinkle and dermal measures at 4 weeks

studies.cite: Ye R, Wang Q, Du L, Li L, Hu F. Topical medium-length PDRN enhances dermal extracellular matrix repair in photodamaged skin via PI3K-Akt/TGF-beta-regulated pathways. PLoS One. 2026;21(7):e0350905.
studies.design: Randomized, double-blind, split-face, self-controlled. 31 healthy women aged 35-55 (mean 47.5), self-reported sensitive skin (Huaxi questionnaire 18-33), periocular lines and eye bags. 0.1% PDRN-850K eye cream versus identical-base 0.1% retinol eye cream, twice daily for 28 days with daily sunscreen. Visits at baseline, day 14 and day 28. Instruments: VISIA 7, Antera 3D, Cutometer, ultrasound. Single site in China; ethics approval September 2025.
studies.who: Healthy Chinese women. Excluded: pregnancy or lactation, systemic or severe skin disease, known allergy to retinol or PDRN, and recent periocular retinoids or nucleic-acid products. Skin tone or Fitzpatrick type is not reported in the text I read.
results: Wrinkles (VISIA image analysis): crow's-feet area and number down about 20-23% at day 28 on the PDRN side versus about 6-7% on the retinol side; similar pattern for infraorbital wrinkles. Benefit appeared by day 14 on the PDRN side.
Dermal structure (ultrasound): dermal thickness and density increased about two-fold more on the PDRN side (authors' description; values in figure 6).
Eye bags and tear trough (Antera 3D): reductions about two-fold greater on the PDRN side.
Elasticity (R2) and firmness (F4): improvements about 1.8-fold higher on the PDRN side.
Tolerability: both creams tolerated; no adverse reactions reported.
studies.effectSize: Statistical results are shown in figure 6 as means with standard errors; the text gives only relative differences (about 1.8 to 2 times) and the wrinkle percentages above. I could not extract p-values or confidence intervals from the text.
studies.placebo: No vehicle-only arm. The comparator is 0.1% retinol, so the study shows PDRN did better than retinol under these conditions, not that PDRN beats a plain moisturiser. Retinol at 0.1% for 4 weeks is also an early readout for retinol.
studies.material: Not established. The instrument differences are measured changes (wrinkle area, ultrasound thickness); no patient-rated outcome or blinded clinician grade is reported in the text I read. The authors warn early ultrasound changes may reflect hydration or plumping.
studies.adverse: None reported in the text I read.
studies.conflict: Authors list affiliations with a skin-aging research institute and a biotechnology company; the PDRN-850K was provided by Ruijiming (Shandong) Biotechnology Co., Ltd., and retinol by DSM-Firmenich. I did not find a funding or competing-interests statement in the text I read; check the paper's front matter.
studies.limits: One trial, 31 people, 4 weeks, one site, eye area only, women only, sensitive-skin cohort. Cell work in 3 experiments. Raman cannot distinguish added from endogenous nucleic acids. In vivo penetration is a single person. Pathway activation was not tested under UV stress. No deep-skin or pigment data.

claimsCheck.status: Direction visible in the paper's figures; but no vehicle arm, 4 weeks, company-linked authors, and a plumping effect not excluded

claimsCheck.claim: Topical PDRN reaches viable skin and dermis
claimsCheck.status: Supportive but indirect: porcine solution at 1000 ppm and a single human volunteer; not shown for a cream in human dermis

products.rankNote: I did not search retail products for this entry. The tested material is not tied to any retail product I found. PDRN products differ in source, fragment length and percentage, so a trial of one preparation does not transfer to another by name alone.

howToUse: Treat as a swap into an existing PDRN or peptide-style repair step, not an extra layer. If the routine has no such step, the evidence is not strong enough to justify adding one on this paper alone.
The tested dose was 0.1% PDRN twice daily around the eyes for 28 days. Face-wide use and other concentrations are untested.
Retinoid interaction is untested. Do not use this paper to drop a prescription retinoid; the comparator was over-the-counter retinol.
Ask the brand for the PDRN percentage, source (salmon or other) and fragment length before paying for a premium version.

expect.what: Probably nothing visible. Check for stinging or redness.
The trial's instruments showed differences from day 14 (authors' reading). Whether you would see or feel it is unknown.
No data. Durability and true remodelling are untested.

dossier.contraindications: Salmon-derived: a fish or salmon allergy is the obvious check (my inference; the trial excluded known PDRN allergy). Pregnancy and breastfeeding were excluded, so no data. No adverse reactions were reported in a sensitive-skin cohort.
dossier.sideBenefits: None shown. The tolerability in sensitive skin is a positive note from a small sample.
wouldChangeVerdict: A vehicle-controlled trial from authors without a commercial link
A longer trial (12 weeks or more) with a prescription-retinoid arm
Data in Fitzpatrick IV-VI and on pigment outcomes
A retail product that discloses a matching PDRN percentage and source
dossier.transfer: The fibroblast pathways studied are not skin-tone specific as far as I know, so the cell-level findings plausibly apply by mechanism. The clinical trial does not: Chinese women, phototype not reported, outcomes were wrinkles and dermal thickness, not pigment or post-inflammatory marks. Do not read this as pigment evidence. I did not search for PDRN trials in pigmentary conditions this run.
